system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. It would reduce our general recovery, shift known risks onto us through disclosure and knowledge provisions, and leave Bluefen, Riverlark and the bonuses unresolved at Completion. We should not accept any of the key positions. Nothing here requires Amelia Frost's approval to reject. Any movement toward the fallback positions (20% cap, 18 months) needs her written authority, which we do not have.

---

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (start); 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority | Starts at our fallback. Reduces recovery by AUD 1.2m. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Five times our threshold. Small claims fall out entirely. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Five times our basket, and only the excess is recoverable. |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with approval) | Shortens the window for latent defects. |
| Limitation applies to all claims | Applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant regimes separate | Lets general limits override other regimes. |
| Title/capacity (Fundamental) | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Core title protection is removed. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims "of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum enforceable extent | No fraud carve-out is visible. Its absence is a serious omission. |
| Disclosure (Sch. 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room and public-register deemed disclosure | Would deem disclosure of everything in 2,000+ pages of material. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for any matter the Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Directly contrary to playbook. Would bar claims on anything in the data room. |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence of conditions satisfied before Completion | Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). DL 2 confirms no final consent exists. |
| Riverlark (2/7) | ~AUD 3.2m facility released after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | DL 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid. We would be funding a secured debt with no release. |
| Bonuses (funds flow; DL 5) | AUD 420,000 excluded from funds flow; "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude | DL 5 confirms they are not in the funds flow and on-costs are unstated. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 unverified | DL 4 says the clause conditions transfer on payment. No receipt is in the data room. |
| Export/privacy incident (4.6/Sch. 6; DL 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand either way | The Seller's characterisation is inconsistent with its own DL 6, which says the investigation is preliminary and scope and notification are unknown. |
| Sandbar renewals (DL 8) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Seller asserts ordinary-course without the disclosure saying so. We need to assess before accepting. |
| Tax/IP (Seller update) | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain open; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | Seller treats them as settled under a regime we have not agreed. |
| Title (DL 10; Seller update) | Share register at DD-012 is evidence of title | Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is an internal supplied source only | The register is the Seller's own document. It does not prove independent title. |

---

## 2. Reasoning on the material issues

**a) Stacked thresholds and caps.** The Seller's mechanics compound. A AUD 200,000 loss with a 25k de minimis and 250k excess-only basket recovers nothing. Our mechanics would recover from the first dollar once the 50k basket is exceeded. The cap and time limit then cut further. The Seller's package is therefore a substantial reduction in recovery, not a presentational change.

**b) Knowledge and disclosure together.** DL 1.1 deems disclosure of every document in the data room. Clause 8.3 then bars claims for anything "discoverable". Combined, the Seller's position would convert the entire diligence record into a disclosure against which we have no warranty claim. This is the most dangerous combination in the draft. We should reject both and require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties.

**c) Fraud carve-out.** The Seller's text applies limitations and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" with no fraud exception. Our playbook requires a carve-out to the maximum enforceable extent. It cannot be waived. This must be inserted, not negotiated.

**d) Title.** Fundamental claims are the most important protection in a share purchase, and the Seller proposes to put them under general limits. Our playbook requires a separate 100% cap and at least six years. Title evidence should come from independent sources (ASIC searches, share transfer history, PPSR, certificates, authority documents), not the Seller's register.

**e) Completion conditions.** Bluefen and Riverlark are both Completion-critical. Bluefen is a material customer with an unresolved change-control clause. "Reasonable endeavours" and "consent on delivery" would let Completion occur before we know whether the customer will continue. Riverlark is secured debt. Completing without repayment and releases leaves the security in place and the debt outstanding. Both should be CP-level items.

**f) Bonuses.** The AUD 420,000 is a known, conditional obligation. The funds flow excludes it, and the disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. If the Seller treats it as "a matter for the Seller", it is still a Company liability if it crystallises at or after Completion. It should be either a specific Completion line item or seller-funded, with on-costs quantified.

**g) Export/privacy incident.** The Seller characterises the matter as immaterial. Its own disclosure says scope, access and notification are unknown, and the export may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. Whether this triggers any notification obligation under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), including the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, is a question for privacy counsel. We should not assume it does or does not. The playbook is to preserve logs, investigate, and require updates, and to avoid any numeric demand before the facts are known.

**h) Ironquay and Sandbar.** The Ironquay indemnity covers only SOW3 and relies on a payment status that is unverified. Broaden it to cover the IP and title position, and keep the SOW3 cure. Sandbar should be assessed on terms, termination rights and timing, not reclassified automatically.

---

## 3. What to push back on

**Reject outright (no authority to accept):**
1. The 20% / AUD 4.8m cap as an opening position. Start at 25% / AUD 6m.
2. The 18-month general claims period. Start at 24 months.
3. Fundamental/title claims under general caps and time limits.
4. Blanket limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to all claims, with no fraud carve-out.
5. Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure.
6. Clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.
7. Bluefen reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
8. Riverlark post-completion release without repayment at Completion.
9. Bonuses excluded from the funds flow.
10. Title proven by the Seller's own share register.
11. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".

**Counter-propose (our playbook positions):**
- General cap 25% / AUD 6m; de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 first-dollar; 24-month general period.
- Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out across all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
- Specific, fair disclosure only. No deemed disclosure of the data room or public registers.
- Delete clause 8.3. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Completion conditions and specific indemnities (require evidence, not assurances):**
- **Bluefen:** Effective written consent and evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Riverlark:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. Any post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded indemnity.
- **Ironquay:** Broadened IP indemnity preserving the SOW3 cure; evidence of SOW3 payment status (the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way).
- **Privacy incident:** Preserve logs, complete the investigation, require written updates before signing, and obtain privacy counsel's view on any notification obligation.
- **Sandbar:** Review the three renewals for terminability, timing and accrued liability. Do not reclassify as Debt automatically.
- **Title:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence.
- **Tax and IP:** Keep open. Do not accept the "settled" characterisation.

**Information requests to the Seller:**
- Bluefen consent and conditions status.
- Riverlark payout letter and draft releases.
- Bonus calculation, payroll tax and superannuation position.
- SOW3 payment records or confirmatory assignment.
- Export incident logs, scope analysis and investigation timetable.
- Sandbar contracts and termination provisions.
- Independent title searches.
- Office lease landlord consent position (DD-007) and Mossvale assignment position (DD-009). The disclosure does not say consent is required, so we should confirm rather than assume.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller's general limitation package.** Restore 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, and 24-month period.
2. **Separate the Fundamental/Title regime** with a 100% cap, six-year period, and no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
3. **Insert a fraud carve-out** across all limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. This is non-negotiable.
4. **Limit disclosure to specific, fair disclosure.** Reject data-room and public-register deemed disclosure.
5. **Delete clause 8.3.** Replace with a qualifier only if named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry apply, and never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
6. **Make Bluefen consent and evidence of satisfied conditions a pre-Completion requirement.**
7. **Require Riverlark repayment and releases at Completion.** Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
8. **Fund the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs** through a specific funds-flow line or seller-funded indemnity.
9. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** while preserving the SOW3 cure.
10. **Investigate the export/privacy incident** without assuming a breach, harm, notification duty or demand. Obtain privacy counsel's advice.
11. **Assess the Sandbar renewals** on their terms, with no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
12. **Keep Tax and IP open** and reject the "settled under the general regime" characterisation.
13. **Require independent title evidence.** The DD-012 register is not sufficient.
14. **Do not offer the 20% cap or 18-month period** without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.

Before sending a mark-up, the deal team should have NSW-qualified transaction counsel review the drafting, and privacy counsel should review the export incident position.
=== END ADVICE ===
